title: 2006 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 4
statement: A dot is marked at each vertex of a triangle \(A B C\). Then, 2,3 , and 7 more dots are marked on the sides \(A B, B C\), and \(C A\), respectively. How many triangles have their vertices at these dots?

solutions.text: Altogether there are \(3+2+3+7=15\) dots, and thus \(\binom{15}{3}=455\) combinations of 3 dots. Of these combinations, \(\binom{2+2}{3}+\binom{2+3}{3}+\binom{2+7}{3}=4+10+84=98\) do not give triangles because they are collinear (the rest do give triangles). Thus \(455-98=357\) different triangles can be formed.
